request: What are the estimated budget costs of clean energy tax credits?

reply.reply: The available official estimate is the original IRA estimate—not a current credits-only total. JCT estimated revenue reductions of $205,231 million over 2022–2031 for all Subtitle D energy-security provisions, a broader category than clean-energy tax credits alone (CRS R47202, PDF p. 29). Within it, the Clean Fuels provisions were estimated to reduce revenues by $18,840 million over 2022–2031 (CRS R47202, PDF p. 27). These are estimates reported in August 2022; the evidence reviewed did not establish a single aggregate for clean-energy tax credits alone or a newer updated aggregate. See the [brief](output/briefs/case-20261025-190140-4ce5.html).
reply.reasoning: The verified evidence supplies original JCT estimates for the broad Subtitle D total and one specific category, but not an aggregate limited to clean-energy tax credits or a newer estimate.
